key_insight: A passing hardware verification test does not guarantee that a design meets its specification. Verify the Verifier uses an LLM to cross-check passing execution traces against the specification, looking for bugs that conventional scoreboards miss.
problem_solved: UVM scoreboards check agreement with a reference model, but incomplete checks or shared mistakes can allow specification violations—called scoreboard escapes—to survive otherwise successful regressions.
method: Analyze traces from passing UVM regressions with an LLM-based Anomaly Cross-Checker.
Ground the cross-check in the design specification to identify violations beyond existing scoreboard checks.
Study 564 inserted bugs across four OpenTitan IPs; the provided abstract mentions 68 candidates but is truncated before reporting complete results.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners building verification tools, this illustrates how specification-grounded LLMs can complement established automated checks. The approach targets hardware verification blind spots rather than treating a passing regression as proof of correctness.
visual_elements: Split-path diagram: execution traces pass the UVM scoreboard but undergo an additional specification-grounded LLM check.
Three-part comparison: design behavior, reference-model expectations, and specification requirements.
Magnifying-glass icon highlighting a hidden specification violation beneath a green test-pass badge.

paper_title: Verify the Verifier: Specification-Grounded LLM Cross-Checking for Bugs That Escape UVM Scoreboards
paper_authors: Ana E. Sanchez Villalobos, Michael D. Quinn, Aakash Tyagi, Minh D. Luu, David Kebo Houngninou
